description: Registry of banned scaffold language in page-three direction output and their approved replacements.

banned_entries.reason: Restates the topic rather than coaching the angle. Generic across all essays. Fails spec Section A.
banned_entries.replacement_family: Direct coaching language scoped to the classified pattern.
examples_banned: Your essay is about what changed when the correction landed — and why the gap existed in the first place.
Your essay is about what you understood after you stopped defending your decision.
Your essay is about the moment when being capable stopped being the same as being responsible.
examples_approved: The real story is the correction, not the activity. At [turningQ], the gap between what you were doing and what was needed became visible.
The conflict is not the story. What you understood after you stopped defending — visible at [turningQ] — is where the essay lives.
At [turningQ], being able to do something stopped being the same as whether you should.

banned_entries.reason: Explains the direction back to itself. Not persuasive. Fails spec Section A.
banned_entries.replacement_family: Persuasive case-specific language that argues why this angle is harder, more specific, and more yours than the generic alternative.
examples_banned: This direction works because it shows a specific gap — not a general lesson.
This direction works because it captures a real moment of growth.
This direction works because the correction is concrete.
examples_approved: Showing a specific correction is harder than claiming growth — the move to [consequenceQ] is what makes this angle non-generic and yours.
Saying what changed after defending yourself is harder than describing the conflict — and it is more specific to you.
Good intentions are common. The moment you understood yours were not enough — in [consequenceQ] — is specific to you.

banned_entries.reason: Procedural instruction that tells the student what to do rather than naming the essay center. Fails spec Section A.
banned_entries.replacement_family: Named essay center with specific chain identification.
examples_banned: Build from the chain where [turningQ] leads to [consequenceQ].
examples_approved: The essay center is the move from [turningQ] to [consequenceQ] — show that chain, not the context around it.

banned_entries.banned_template: This version overweights setup and underweights the real decision.
banned_entries.reason: Judgment template that applies identically to all runner-up candidates regardless of actual case content. Fails spec Section A.
banned_entries.replacement_family: Case-specific language about what this path misses.
examples_banned: This version overweights setup and underweights the real decision.
examples_approved: This path stays in context and misses the moment that makes the essay specific.

banned_entries.banned_template: This version keeps the decision and consequence tied to one clear thread.
banned_entries.reason: Approval template that applies identically regardless of what the actual stronger thread is. Fails spec Section A.
banned_entries.replacement_family: Case-specific language about why the winning read wins.
examples_banned: This version keeps the decision and consequence tied to one clear thread. The stronger read wins because it gives you a clear essay center and a concrete move to draft from.
examples_approved: This version centers the real decision — the one your notes make specific to you.

enforcement_notes: All banned templates were audited in direction.ts on 2026-03-24.
Pattern matching for essayAboutnessClarity scoring was updated to recognize the new approved language families.
The banned templates were fully removed from all code paths in deriveThemeStatement(), deriveWhyStatement(), buildRuntimeCandidates(), and deriveCoachComparison().
Future additions to direction.ts must not reintroduce template language from the banned_entries list.
